capabilities.target: user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start and injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Recalled memories, which can contain content originally written from untrusted web sources via memory.save, are explicitly instructed to be treated as the user's own instructions, with no re-verification of origin or authority. This is the design's root cause: trust is granted to persisted content regardless of how it entered memory.

No restriction is given on what counts as 'useful' preference or standing instruction to save; any content the model judges useful, including attacker-supplied text encountered while researching, qualifies for persistence.

The entire memory trust and scope boundary is enforced purely through natural-language instructions to the model. No structural validation, provenance tagging, or human review is described anywhere in the design.

controls.name: Memory write provenance tagging and trust-level propagation
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the data store itself rather than by the model, the provenance tag persists regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Treat recalled memory as untrusted reference data, not as user instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Structural separation of recalled memory into a clearly delimited, non-instruction channel narrows the path, but a more capable or adversarially prompted model can still elect to act on content it recognizes as plausible instructions.

controls.name: Human approval gate, raw action review, before any mail.send call
Scope drive.read credential to task-relevant folders instead of the entire drive
Periodic human review and audit of saved memory entries

findings.title: Lethal trifecta via memory laundering (TC5 chained into TC1): poisoned web content persists as trusted instructions, driving confidential drive read and email exfiltration

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled web page fetched during research contains hidden instructions or framed 'preferences'.
Agent saves the content verbatim via memory.save, per prompt.md:2-3's unscoped instruction to save 'anything useful', with no filtering.
Entry persists across sessions with no provenance tag and no human review (runtime notes).
At the next session start the poisoned entry is injected into the system prompt and, per prompt.md:4, is explicitly treated as the user's own instructions.
Acting on the injected 'instruction', the agent reads the user's full, confidential drive.
Agent sends the retrieved confidential content to an attacker-chosen address via mail.send, which has no approval gate and can send to any address.

evidence.observation: Instruction explicitly directs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, with no distinction for content that originated from untrusted web sources.
Agent is instructed to save 'anything useful' to memory via memory.save with no filtering, validation, or scope restriction on what is saved.
memory.save accepts free text, there is no provenance on memory entries, and the user never reviews them, so poisoned content is indistinguishable from legitimate preferences.
mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files, completing the exfiltration path.

recommendations.action: Tag every memory entry with its originating trust level at write time, enforced by the memory store itself, and never promote untrusted-tagged content to instruction status on recall.
Present recalled memory to the model as untrusted reference data inside clearly delimited tags, never merged into the system prompt as directives.
Require human approval with raw-action review (full recipient address and body shown, not a collapsed summary) before any mail.send call.
Scope drive.read to the minimum folder set needed per task instead of the entire drive.

findings.title: Unprovenanced, unreviewed memory writes create a persistent, unaudited instruction channel

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content read during research.
Saved verbatim with no provenance tag and no human review (runtime notes), and no scope limit (prompt.md:2-3).
Resulting store entry is indistinguishable from a legitimate user preference and is not auditable to its untrusted origin.

forecast.watch_signal: Any new tool, MCP server integration, or drive/mailbox scope expansion added to this agent without first adding memory provenance tagging and a recall trust boundary; the already-poisoned memory automatically extends its reach to each new capability.

evidence.observation: memory.save accepts free text; there is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.
Agent is told to save 'anything useful' without scope or validation criteria, so any future tool connected to this agent inherits whatever has already been planted in memory.

recommendations.action: Log and periodically surface saved memory entries, with their origin, for user review and revocation.
Before connecting any new tool or data source to this agent, re-run this assessment; the existing memory channel will extend to the new capability by default.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach the critical inherent tier: untrusted web content reaches an irreversible, unapproved egress action (email send carrying confidential drive content) through an unprovenanced memory store that the system prompt explicitly instructs the agent to treat as the user's own authority (prompt.md:4). No control in this design has status declared or verified; every plausible mitigation (provenance tagging, a non-instruction recall boundary, an approval gate on email, drive scope limiting, memory audit) is absent, so residual risk equals inherent risk at critical with no credit applied per rubric section 5. The forecast does not need a trigger to reach a worse tier than the present state, because there is no decaying control left to defeat; it remains critical, and the single most consequential gap to close is the absence of any approval gate on cap.email_send combined with the instruction that collapses the trust boundary between untrusted memory and user authority (prompt.md:4). Closing that one line, with structural provenance tagging on memory.save, would be the highest-leverage fix.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP config, or agent card was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact permission boundary of drive.read) is inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on specific paths is medium rather than high.

No explicit autonomy or step/runtime limit configuration was provided; autonomy level and step limits are inferred as unbounded from the absence of any stated limit, which is what triggers the autonomy modifier in rubric section 4.
